paper.title: A deep-cut bisection envelope algorithm for fixed points (Algorithm 825)
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 29(3), p. 309 (Sep 2003), per the frame item and the shipped 825.gz shar header
paper.url: https://netlib.org/toms/825.gz (article not fetched; ACM page not used)

code.commit: netlib CALGO archive 825.gz (shell archive dated 2003-10-24; C/Src/src.c, C/Drivers/driver.c, C/Drivers/bigtest.res, C/Drivers/smalltest.res, Doc/readme)
code.archive: downloaded by scout 2026-11-27 from netlib.org/toms/825.gz (HTTP 200, 7160 bytes). sha256 of 825.gz: b28e369b226302276dfb83188d493c3029ebfca1714f66123495015b5dbf9b07 (scout download, 2026-11-27).
code.note: Gunzip the archive, then unpack the shell archive with /bin/sh in an empty directory (the shar begins at the #! /bin/sh line). Build C/Src/src.c with C/Drivers/driver.c using a C compiler, run the driver from C/Drivers, answer 1 at its first prompt (the large test), and compare the printed BEFix block with the shipped C/Drivers/bigtest.res.

field: numerics (bisection-type fixed-point and root methods, envelope algorithm)

claim.location: Shipped reference output C/Drivers/bigtest.res (inside 825.gz), first block 'BEFix residual criterion method, epsilon = 0.000100, q = 1.000000', line 42: 'average number of evaluations = 20.417255'. The driver runs the large test (65025 tests) of the BEFix method at that epsilon and reports the mean number of function evaluations.

reference.sha256: not computed for the member; the value is quoted here and compared as a number

claim.paper_value: Value 20.417255 at line 42 of the shipped bigtest.res, as printed by the shipped driver (6 decimals). The paper's table is not read; the claim is the code's own printed output.
claim.metric: The 'average number of evaluations' printed for the first (BEFix) block of the regenerated large-test output, compared as an absolute number with the shipped value
claim.determinism: deterministic (the large test enumerates a fixed grid of 65025 cases; no random numbers)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The shipped value is printed to 6 decimals, so the print rounding alone is up to 5e-7; 1e-6 covers that and nothing more. The mean is over an integer count of evaluations, so a faithful build must reproduce it exactly. A changed bisection step, a different stopping rule or an off-by-one in the evaluation count moves the mean by far more than 1e-6. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 5 minutes: one C build and one driver run over 65025 cases (the shipped test is small, 0.03 s per thousand evaluations expected).
cost.data_size: None (the test cases are generated inside the driver).
cost.data_licence: Netlib CALGO archive; licence per the archive's own notices (the rerun should record it).

why: The shipped large test runs the BEFix bisection on a full grid of cases and prints a mean evaluation count that the code must compute, so the rerun has to execute the C method to reproduce it.
